However, the practical application of existing thermal compounds is limited by the insufficient heat transfer pathways and usage of extremely high-filler loading. This affects the processability and synergistic effect of nanocomposites and consequently deterioration in mechanical properties. To improve the distribution and orientation of the fillers, here we have used a spray coating followed by hot pressing method with the help of exfoliated hexagonal boron nitride nanosheets (h-BNNS) with the aspect ratio ~130 is used as filler in the ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) matrix. The thermal management application for the composite film was demonstrated with the help of a 10 W light-emitting diode bulb. It was found that the thermal compound film with the addition of 15 wt.% h-BNNS shows the surface temperature reduction by~9 °C compared to the pure EVA matrix. This work provides a simple, scalable, and high heat-spreading thermal compound composite that may be used for next-generation heat dissipation in consumer electronics.

articleTitle: Digital twin in manufacturing: Transient Thermo-Mechanical Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: The Digital Twin (DT) has received a lot of research attention and discussion in recent years. It contributes significantly to the industry's transition from the conventional era of trial and error to the contemporary industrial mode. Simulation and computer-aided engineering (CAE) are important components of the DT concept. Manufacturing DT is a virtual representation of the actual processes that may be planned for and enhanced. Additionally, DT offers an infinite number of measurement points and variables without using large, expensive sensors during the actual process.Surface mount technology (SMT) components are frequently attached to printed circuit boards (PCB) using reflow soldering. Employing DT in manufacturing, will end up in reduction in production time and cost, and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions from the production line.In this article, a Digital Twin based multiphysics model is used, powered by the Ansys simulation environment, to conduct a comprehensive virtual analysis of the reflow process from both thermo-fluid dynamic and structural perspectives. Thermo-fluid dynamic results are coupled to a structural analysis tool to simulate the stresses and possible deformations during the reflow process. Thermo-fluid dynamic and structural simulation results were compared against the experimental test results done in the Nokia Factory in Oulu, Finland.

articleTitle: Effect of Isothermal Aging on Anisotropic Creep Properties of SAC305 Single Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Predicting life of SAC305 solder joints in service is difficult as many Sn-based solder materials may undergo microstructural evolution depending on the loading conditions. Aging of solder joint at even room temperature can change the microstructure of the solder material, affecting its properties and fatigue durability of solder joints. SAC solder joints are well known to contain few grains (oligocrystalline). Due to this, accurate estimation of thermo-mechanical properties of single SAC crystal and grain boundaries is required, to model grain-scale solder joint response under life-cycle loading. Multitier microstructure-based crystal-viscoplasticity (CV) modelling of oligocrystalline SAC solder joint, based on fundamental dislocation mechanics, developed by this research group, is used for predictive modeling. During isothermal aging of solder joints, both the pro-eutectic β-Sn dendrites as well as the eutectic regions undergo thermal evolution. In addition, under the presence of cyclic mechanical stresses at temperature, grain and grain boundaries may also continuously evolve. In microstructure-sensitive modeling, it is important to determine the contribution of each of these microstructural features so that accurate modelling of anisotropic behavior of oligocrystalline solder joints can be conducted for more accurate prediction of their fatigue durability.In this paper, single-crystal high aspect ratio (HAR) SAC305 solder joints are fabricated with appropriate cooling rate, and then subjected to isothermal aging, to capture the effects of such microstructural aging on microstructural evolution and resulting evolution of creep resistance of single SAC crystals. Monocrystalline morphology and grain orientation are determined from microscopy and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). Features <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">being tracked within the grain are Ag</sup>3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Sn IMC particle</sup> size and spacing in the eutectic region and the area fraction of the pro-eutectic β-Sn dendritic region.Samples are aged at 125°C for 0, 100 and 300 hrs., for studying the effect of isothermal aging. Scanning electron microscope and image processing are used to study microstructural evolution. Room temperature creep tests are conducted on single crystal solder joints. Future paper will report the associated electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) for grain orientation measurement and the creep modelling (using CV model), to determine the effect of the microstructural aging on anisotropic creep (Hill-Garofalo) model constants. These calibrated continuum model constants will be used to conduct thermomechanical simulations of QFN package to investigate the effect of isothermal aging on the fatigue durability of solder interconnects.

articleTitle: Shear Strength Analysis of Aging SAC-Bi Solder Joints with Different Solder Paste Volumes
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: The occurrence of solder joint failures frequently constrains the reliability of electronic assemblies. Ball shear testing is widely used to evaluate solder joint strength quantitatively. Several factors, such as surface finish, solder alloy composition, shear rate, etc., play a substantial role in determining both shear strength and failure modes in a solder joint. This study aims to investigate the impact of aging on the shear properties of SAC-Bi alloys under different solder paste volumes. The test specimens were assembled by attaching Sn-3Ag-3Bi-0.8Cu-Ni paste to SAC305 solder spheres with an 18-mil diameter. The assembly process involved stencil heights of 4, 5, and 6 mils and incorporated an organic solderability preservatives (OSP) surface finish (SF). The aging process occurred under two distinct temperature conditions: 75 and 125 °C, with aging periods of 100 hours and 1000 hours, respectively. The test results were compared to those of a control sample kept at a room temperature of 25 °C. Shear testing was executed at a controlled strain rate of 0.01 mm/sec, and eight tests were performed for each combination. Shear strength and shear energy were determined by generating and analyzing shear stress-strain curves for each test. Microstructure analysis of the sheared solder joints was performed using optical microscopy to identify the changes due to the increased solder paste volume. The results indicated a substantial reduction in shear strength as aging advanced while the shear energy increased with higher temperatures. Furthermore, it was observed that the impact of aging on shear strength and shear energy decreased as the solder paste volume increased. Additionally, it was observed that as the solder paste volume increased, the impact of aging on shear strength and shear energy decreased.

articleTitle: Increasing Cooling Performance of Phase Change Materials with Metal Foam Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Phase change materials (PCM) serve to maintain constant surface temperatures, crucial for preventing thermal failures in electronic components subjected to increasing heat fluxes. PCM, integrated with efficient heat sink structures, offers local cooling to safeguard devices. Passive cooling solutions, such as PCM-based systems, require no energy consumption or complex mechanical parts. The melting-solidification cycle of PCM stores and releases energy within a specific temperature range, ensuring constant temperature operation, particularly in time-dependent scenarios. PCM stabilizes and regulates component temperatures under cyclic heat loads, extending operational lifespan for steady loads by averting critical temperature thresholds. Considering the low thermal conductivity of PCM (<1 W/mK), strategies such as the use of metal fins (PCM heat sinks), incorporation of high thermal conductivity nanoparticles, or utilization of metal foam matrices as thermal conductivity enhancers (TCE) are proposed. This study investigates the thermal performance of PCM integrated with metal foam structures and fins to prevent IC package temperature failures. The experimental study utilized variable parameters such as metal foam porosity (0.88–0.94), pores per inch (PPI) values (10-20-40), and heat loads (20-40 W). Thermal performance comparisons between heatsink and metal foam structures are conducted, establishing a foundation for using metal foam-PCM composites.

articleTitle: Use of Functionalized Nanodiamond Additive for Enhancement of Thermal Convective Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In electrical infrastructure, transformer systems are a key link the power supply chain. The throughput capacity of these systems is largely limited by its core temperature, driven by resistive heating and mitigated by the thermal characteristics of the transformer’s oil. If the transformer oil’s thermal conductivity can be improved without significant sacrifice of other characteristics, then more heat can be wicked away for the same temperature gradients, naturally allowing for lowered core temperatures or increased throughput power capacity if core temperature is to be held as constant. Several additive approaches have been taken in course of this goal; however, this study focuses on use of nanoscale diamonds functionalized with oleic acid as a potential method of enhancement. Diamond structures are dielectric and have an exceptionally high thermal conductivity (~2,200 W/m•K), making them theoretically ideal as an additive in electronics thermal management. This study focuses on the thermal behavior of transformer oil with 0.2 wt% to 1.0 wt% functionalized nanodiamond additive. Tests occur within a controlled natural convection environment with a target hot surface temperature of 60 °C. Thermal convection coefficients are empirically calculated via energy balance and heat flux methods. Temperature differentials at steady-state are used as well as a measure of enhancement.

articleTitle: Accelerating Thermal Analysis of Chiplet Designs by Embedding FANTASTIC BCI-ROMs in CFD models
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Embedding Boundary Condition Independent Reduced Order Models (BCI-ROMs) of chiplets inside a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation of a package greatly accelerates thermal simulation workflows while completely obfuscating any sensitive intellectual property associated with the original chiplet design. The paper will describe the workflow to create embeddable BCI-ROMs of chiplets and assemble them in a full thermal CFD model of a package. The resultant model is analyzed in a transient power step scenario and results compared to the full 3D high-fidelity equivalent model. Implications of this approach for the chiplet thermal model supply chain will be discussed.

articleTitle: Power Supply Unit Cooling in a High Heat Capture Ratio Liquid Cooled Datacenter Server
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Liquid cooling is a promising cooling solution for datacenter servers to achieve good energy efficiency. A better energy efficiency can be achieved with a higher heat capture ratio(HCR) by liquid. Existing liquid cooling solution for a power supply unit (PSU) in a high HCR liquid cooled server is too expensive to be adopted. This paper provides component level and server system level cooling solution for the PSU in a high HCR liquid cooled server by attaching an air-to-liquid heat exchanger(HEX) to the exit of an existing air-cooled PSU without any changes to the internal design of the existing air-cooled PSU. The proposed PSU cooling solution in a high HCR liquid cooled server can decrease the cooling solution cost by 60%~65% as compared to the existing cold plate liquid cooled PSU solution, and it is free of liquid leaks issue within the server since the air-to-liquid HEX is outside of the server chassis. The component level HEX is scaled for server and rack level heat dissipation with a server level universal HEX and shown to operate with a very high efficiency of 87.5% even without the use of cold air aisle that is used in the traditional rear door heat exchanger.

Author Keywords: compact crossflow universal rear mounted heat exchanger(CCU-RMHX)

articleTitle: Novel Programmable Package-level 3D Thermal Evaluation System
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Thermal management of semiconductor chips continues to be a very critical topic in the industry. It is necessary to evaluate/manage the thermal aspects of a chip throughout the development cycle – starting from initial planning stage to beyond customer board deployment. In this paper, we present a versatile 3D thermal evaluation vehicle that can serve as an important tool in addressing the above requirement. This paper describes the architecture, implementation, details of operation, programming aspects, usage model and various applications of a silicon chip that will be used as a 3D thermal evaluation tool. The methodology of 3D thermal evaluation for usage in the package development process is addressed. While having a simple implementation and usage model – this chip provides considerable 3D thermal evaluation capabilities. The usage model includes the following:•3D modelling of thermal behavior of semiconductor chips to evaluate architecture/floorplan – while the chips are still in development phase•Cross-calibrating 3D thermal simulators with chip-level measurement data•Evaluating various aspects for package development - including thermal interface materials•Studying customer use power-maps to evaluate cooling solutionsThe chip interfaced with a simple test-platform has ability to do automated on-chip measurements. Silicon measurement data is presented and compared to simulation results based on numerical models. It is concluded that this evaluation system can play a critical role in the 3D thermal evaluation and management of a semiconductor chip throughout its development cycle. The results from this eval system are applicable to 2D and 3D packages.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Encapsulated Flexible Hybrid Electronic Assemblies Under Board-Level Drop Test
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Flexible-hybrid electronics (FHE) are gaining increasing traction in consumer electronics. This surge in the popularity of FHE can be attributed to the capacity to conform to diverse shapes in addition to weight reduction and a slim profile. The FHEs need to be encapsulated using encapsulants to mitigate the effects of shock loads. Most of the prior research on FHE is focused on the printing process development and process performance. The reliability of the FHEs under drop and vibration is not well understood. This paper focuses on the assessment of the survivability of direct-write additive printed electronics, the evaluation of the reliability of encapsulants in promoting drop-survivability, and the analysis of the failure modes in encapsulated additively printed FHE. In this paper, FHE circuits are printed using a direct write platform and encapsulated to improve reliability, followed by board-level drop testing. The boards are tested at a G-level of 40G, typical of automotive applications. The number of shock events to failure has been assessed for the FHEs, and the reliability of the various encapsulant materials has been investigated. The failed samples have been analyzed to understand the specific failure modes. The study could have practical implications for manufacturers developing FHEs for consumer and harsh environmental applications, and it provides valuable insights into the survivability and failure modes of encapsulated FHEs.

articleTitle: Constitutive Behaviors of Sn58Bi, Sn57Bi-1Ag and other Low Temperature Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In this study, we report the mechanical behavior of two low-temperature solder joints formed with Sn58Bi and Alloy-4 on Organic Solderability Preservative (OSP) surface finish. The comprehensive testing is aimed at developing constitutive models for a variety of low-temperature solder (LTS) alloys including Sn58Bi, Sn57Bi-1Ag, 42SnBi-0.5Sb, and Alloy-4. Towards this end, we report preliminary test results on Sn57Bi-1Ag 42SnBi-0.5Sb alloys. The investigation utilizes double lap-shear mechanical tests conducted using a custom-made closed-loop capacitively controlled sub-micron precision mechanical tester. In total, nine monotonic tests and nine creep tests were conducted for each material at three different temperatures. Monotonic tests were carried out at three different strain rates, ranging from 7.7 * 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> to 7.7 * 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, while creep tests were conducted at three stress levels, ranging from 5.17 MPa to 20.69 MPa. The data obtained from these tests will be utilized to derive viscoplastic constitutive models including the Anand model, the power-law creep model, and the time-hardening primary-secondary creep model. Using the experimental data, we discuss the following aspects: 1) creep and monotonic testing results under various conditions to understand the constitutive behavior of four alloys 2) aging effect on the tested alloys to understand how their properties evolve over time.

articleTitle: Unsteady state numerical study and analysis of Boron Doped Diamond as heat spreader in a laptop form-factor for cooling the SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In today’s world, there is always a need to demand more power from the System on Chip (SoC) due to the ever-increasing concurrency of work to be done at the same point in time. To meet this demand, the heat dissipation from the SOC or processor needs to be removed with better materials that have higher conductivity and, at the same time, lower density and higher specific heat capacity. Having a lower density helps to have an optimal weight for the power dissipation ratio. The Boron Doped Diamond (BDD) is a better choice than traditionally used high-conductivity materials such as Copper (Cu). The BDD material used for our study is made using Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD). The BDD-CVD material has roughly 2-5 times the conductivity of copper and thus helps us with better heat transfer both in steady-state and transient-state conditions. This benefits us in either achieving increased power for a particular duration or, for the same power, increasing the time duration of running a workload before it reaches the temperature limits that are deemed safe to operate the device. The temperature limits can be those of the SoC and the skins of the device. The laptops have different surfaces, and they have different temperature limits deemed to be safe to maintain them for the ergonomic compliance of the end user. The BDD-CVD material, though popularly not used for heat spreading now, can be one of the high-conductivity materials that can be used to benefit the above-mentioned cooling applications in the future.

articleTitle: Experimental and Numerical Investigation of Thermal Performance of Piezoelectric Fan
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Electronic cooling ensures the smooth operation of electroning components without degradation. It is seen that the local heat loads become critical as the minimization of electronic components. More smaller sizes of integrated circuits and the low heat transfer areas aggravate removing of excess heat with conduction and traditional cooling. Since conduction of heat is significantly difficult in such cases, applications based on local cooling with forced convection or phase change can be a useful solution. The most commonly used forced convection cooling method is using fans. While fans offer many advantages, they also come with additional issues such as power consumption, vibration, reliability, noise, and vibrations. Instead of inconvenient applications which cause high noise and power consumption, piezoelectric units used like fan can be employed. This type of fans, designed using piezoelectric materials, are effectively utilized in chip-focused cooling. By exciting piezoelectric materials to resonance, the vibration generated allows the steel structure at the tip to oscillate at a certain rate that resonance frequency of the piezoelectric fan system. This causes airflow with low power consumption with regard to a using a centrifugal fan. In this study, the numerical analysis of a piezoelectric fan designed for cooling a chip with a 5W heat load was experimentally validated. After validation, numerical analyses were conducted in the ANSYS Fluent program for five different frequency values (60,80,114,140,170Hz) and four tip displacements (3.5, 6.5, 10, 15mm), investigating the impact of these parameters on cooling performance. Numerical analyses are validated by using experimental results. 4 different experiments are conducted with two different experimental setups. In the first setup, heatsink is used for validating the numerical study. In the second setup, piezo connection type, blade length and voltage connection parameters are investigated. As a result, the use of piezoelectric fans, with their advantages of being quiet and compact in local cooling applications, can provide temperature drop. In the numerical studies, it was determined that a specific frequency value provided the most ideal thermal performance, and beyond a certain point, the effect of frequency on cooling performance did not change linearly. Additionally, it is found that the tip displacement also improves the thermal performance with relatively low improvement rate.

articleTitle: Altering Electromigration Response in Aluminum Wire Bonds through Heat Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In this study, a control group of aluminum wire bonds attached to direct bond copper pads are subjected to electromigration conditions of 57,000 [A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>] at an ambient homologous temperature of 0.5 [K/K] (194 [°C]). Treatment groups in this study subjected wire bonded cards to heat treatment prior to electromigration stressing. The four treatments consisted of one- or 24-hour durations at homologous ambient temperatures of 0.45 or 0.55 [K/K]. The results show a negative relationship between electromigration lifetime and wire length in both the control and treatment groups. Heat treatment groups show increased electrical resistivity, indicating increased sensitivity to wire length with respect to electromigration lifetime. Standard deviation of heat treatment groups is also notably larger than that of the control group, indicating that extended periods of time at homologous temperatures in the 0.45 to 0.55 range reduce the quality of high-purity aluminum wire bonded regions but do not necessarily indicate a reduced lifetime. Additional examination of the effects of wire length on thermal-electric failure modes is examined and discussed in relation to the aforementioned observations.

articleTitle: Evaluation and analysis of role of tonal noise components on overall noise of portable notebook PC blowers
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: With notebook PC’s becoming compact and computationally powerful, the focus on the performance augmentation and use of high-performance blowers have increased exponentially in recent decades to meet the cooling targets while maintaining acceptable temperatures. One of the focus areas is to reduce the overall noise of blowers to have better end user experience in terms of acoustic ergonomics without compromising the cooling capabilities. Blowers are the key noise source when deployed to cool system, which have powers beyond passive cooling capabilities. The noise associated with blowers have both tonal components (narrow band noise) and broadband components. The tonal components are highly annoying as it sounds shrill while the broadband noise, in combination with tonal components, increases the overall sound pressure level (SPL). Psychoacoustics parameters like tonality and prominence ratio help to quantify the annoyance perceived from tonal noise.In this paper, the contribution of tonal noise components on overall noise is discussed for blowers of portable notebook system. The blowers are tested in anechoic chamber as per ECMA-74 standards using state of the art equipment. The tones are detected based on criteria set by Terhardt/Aures using MATLAB. The tone contribution on overall noise is evaluated and discussed in detail. The tones are observed to have very less contribution towards overall noise at higher SPL (A) values for the current generation notebook blowers. The observations obtained in this work implies that to reduce the overall noise of portable notebook blowers the solutions or ideas that reduces broadband component shall be targeted rather than tonal noise as long as the blower tonal noise contribution is low.

articleTitle: Comparison of Single and Dual Orifice Synthetic Jets for Flow Structure and Heat Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Synthetic jets have garnered considerable attention in electronics thermal management due to their notable attributes, including compactness, low energy consumption, cost-effectiveness, and user convenience. Numerous rigorous studies have delved into the characteristic parameters of both single-orifice and multiple-orifice synthetic jet devices to comprehend heat transfer and flow physics for a wide range of applications. This study focuses on investigating the heat transfer capability of a dual-orifice synthetic jet over a single-orifice synthetic jet to address space constraint. An SST k-ω turbulence model with a commercially available CFD software (ANSYS Fluent) was used to investigate the thermal and fluidic behavior of a single-orifice synthetic jet and a dual-orifice synthetic jet. The current study explored the effects of varying widths of two orifices and the spacing between them. By utilizing an identical cavity and equal excitation parameters, results indicate an approximate 4% additional reduction in the average temperature of the heated surface when employing a dual-orifice synthetic jet configuration. Moreover, the dual-orifice synthetic jet exhibited a 6% higher average heat transfer coefficient compared to a conventional synthetic jet, while the performances of the other two configurations of dual-orifice synthetic jets were surpassed by a single-orifice synthetic jet. These outcomes can be attributed to the variation of jet interactions introduced by different dual-orifice configurations.

articleTitle: CFD Evaluation of Electrochemical Additively Manufactured Heat Sinks for Single-Phase Immersion Cooling
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: As the power-density of high-performance electronics continues to increase, the demand for efficient cooling solutions is critical to maintaining performance and reliability. Conventional thermal management equipment and strategies are steadily approaching the limits of their viability. To address this, research in academia and industry is assessing various emergent cooling technologies that allow for future growth and further scaling of electronics power-densities. Of these, single-phase immersion cooling (SPIC) enables a substantial performance leap while offering simplicity and reliability. Novel additive manufacturing (AM) technologies offer new fabrication methods that can revolutionize electronics heat sink design and manufacturing, by permitting complex geometries that were previously unattainable. In this study, heat sinks designed for electrochemical additive manufacturing (ECAM) with Body Centered Cubic (BCC) lattice structures are evaluated using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) conjugate heat transfer (CHT) analyses in ANSYS Fluent for single-phase immersion cooling applications. More complex heat sink cooling surface geometries enabled by ECAM fabrication technologies have a greater surface area to volume ratio than traditional parallel plate fins. To benchmark performance, we establish a baseline immersion cooling heat sink metric for various dielectric fluid flowrates using a conventional finned heat sink. We then compare the thermal resistance and pressure drop characteristics of this baseline with those of the ECAM BCC lattice heat sink design. Additional design factors of wall thickness and porosity are also considered. This study evaluates the thermal performance of ECAM-fabricated BCC lattice heat sinks as an innovative solution for enhancing cooling efficiency in high power-density electronics immersion cooling applications. The findings are expected to offer valuable insights into the viability and performance advantages of such heat sinks. By leveraging the capabilities of AM designed structures, this research contributes to the development of more effective and sustainable immersion cooling solutions for next-generation electronic systems.

articleTitle: Characterization of Phase Change Thermal Interface Material Pre-conditioning by Enabling High-Temperature Pressure Mapping Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: All electronic components generating a high amount of heat require external cooling solutions to keep device temperatures within specified limits, ensuring optimal performance and reducing degradation over time. For microprocessors, a heatsink utilizing either heat pipe technology or vapor chambers is commonly used to cool the package in combination with a Thermal Interface Material (TIM). In some instances, a Phase Change TIM (PCTIM) is the preferred type - for example, when relatively low mechanical pressure on the TIM must suffice, but very low TIM thermal resistance cannot be compromised by using thermal gap fillers or gap pads.For Personal Computing (PC) cooling applications, PCTIM has some advantages that may improve the thermal design performance. However, to benefit from these advantages, it is imperative to understand how the heatsink load and pressure over the die are affected when the PCM TIM is heated beyond its phase change temperature threshold (or activation temperature), and subsequently cooled back down to room temperature. Some of the advantages that can be obtained when the heatsink-TIM design is properly characterized are: 1) Reliability: no flow-out or pump-out, in other words, no migration of TIM outside the contacting surfaces that creates voids and reduces performance. 2) Adherence: after a pre-heat process activates or "pre-conditions" the PCTIM, it flows providing good surface coverage and resulting in a well-adhered thermal joint. 3) High thermal conductivity and low thermal resistance: testing showed that a PCTIM could be up to 10% better than traditional high-performance greases.In this paper, the authors present how a pre-load and temperature profiling methodology was qualified to optimize surface wetting and to achieve a thin TIM bond line thickness and correspondingly low thermal resistance. This was done using a realistic, system-like test setup, capturing real-time loads and pressures with a high-temperature pressure-mapping sensor and direct heating from silicon test chips. As the material is heated and starts flowing, the pressure-mapping sensor was used to capture the load and pressure changes over the entire heating area. Simultaneously, embedded sensors on the silicon test chip were used to generate an accurate temperature profile across the die area.The new methodology allowed the team to measure the performance of PCTIM at thicknesses between 20-50μm, a range in which they are seen to be competitive with leading high-performance grease TIM options. As a result, it was possible to show steady-state and transient thermal improvement using this metrology for the current generation of heatsinks and test chips. More importantly, the methodology provides valuable insight into the interplay between various design parameters such as heatsink load and pressure distribution on the TIM, initial versus final thickness after pre-conditioning, and achieved TIM thermal resistance. Although PCTIMs are not new in the market, testing and validation in realistic system conditions using advanced methodologies such as the one described here are key enablers of optimized cooling designs for future high-performance systems.

articleTitle: Study of Aluminum Foam Material For Heat Dissipation of Heat Source at Varying Heat Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: An experimental study was conducted to test the heat dissipation capabilities of aluminum foam in both a forced convection system, where the velocities vary, and a latent heat system involving phase change material (PCM). Throughout all of the testing, surrogate cylindrical heating sources were utilized to vary the amount of heat generated. These experiments were performed to determine the best evolution of cooling practices that could later be applied to cylindrical battery cells. Surrogate heat sources were used in place of battery cells to prevent any dangerous degradation and overheating that are well known to occur. Initially, the surrogate heat source was placed in a matrix of aluminum foam and allowed to cool by natural convection. This was later improved upon by exposing the system to forced convection. Furthermore, smaller-scale aluminum foam samples were subsequently utilized to test the varying pore per inch (PPI) characteristic with PCM. It was found how both the aluminum foam helped increase the PCM's effective thermal conductivity and how the PCM aided the aluminum foam in absorbing the generated heat. The experimental study demonstrated the benefit of solely using aluminum foam and forced convection to dissipate generated heat over the traditional air-cooling system as well as the effect that varying PPI values of aluminum foam had on the heat transfer capabilities of metal foam-enhanced phase change material composites.

articleTitle: Cold Plate Liquid Cooling Solution for Hot-swapped Components in Server System
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: With the explosive growth in demand for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine leaning(ML), the CPU/GPU Thermal Design Power(TDP) is continuous increasing generation by generation in server system. Liquid cooling solution is becoming irreplaceable solution with its benefit of energy usage efficiency compared with air cooling system in current datacenter server systems. The cold plate liquid cooling solution is widely used in industry to deal with increasing system level cooling challenges with improved Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). For a cold plate liquid cooling server system, the ideal solution would be all components in the server can be liquid cooled in order to get 100% heat capture ratio(HCR). In the real products, the main components such as CPU/memories can be liquid cooled, but other components such as IO card, SSD may still be air cooled. There are many technical challenges to use liquid cooling cold plate to cover these components for many reasons, such as mechanical limitation, different form factors, hot swap requirement etc. This paper proposes a total thermal/mechanical cold plate cooling solution to solve such challenges in SSD and IO module with various form factor and hot swapped demand. Two-piece parts of cooling solution are designed. One part with heat pipe embedded in the hot swapped components and one part with liquid channel cold plate. With two parts docking mechanism, the cooling path from hot components to the liquid is created. The thermal analysis and mechanical design concept are introduced in this paper. A prototype sample in the POC (proof of concept) project is tested to verify the concept and solution. The proposed cooling solution can keep the target components within their thermal spec and meet close to 100% heat capture to liquid cooling loop, which maximizes the energy efficiency for the cold plate liquid cooling server.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Single-phase Immersion Cooling of a Single Server and a Cluster of Servers in a Tank
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Immersion cooling of IT equipment is a key liquid cooling technology. The industry now has many commercial implementations of both single-phase immersion cooling using mineral oils and two-phase immersion cooling using engineered fluids such as hydrofluroethers (HFEs) and fluoroketones (FK). Immersion cooling has the benefit of cooling the entirety of the server and does not require additional plumbing within the server equipment. Immersion cooling can provide many of the benefits of water cooling while minimizing the risk and damage associated with water leaks. In this paper we will firstly provide an overview of developments in the industry and technology and then discuss the simulation assessment of i) a single mineral oil immersion cooled 2U server with 2 processors and 4 GPUs and ii) a cluster of mineral oil cooled 2U servers in a tank. The server level simulations will compare the temperatures of key components and flow profiles within the server for a baseline air-cooled server as well as a mineral oil cooled server at different flow velocities. The tank level simulations will focus on tank level simulations of a cluster of oil immersion cooled servers in a large tank. The results show the thermal and flow profiles that are set up within the tank at different bulk pumping rates. The simulations will also explore the impact of server removal for servicing on flow and cooling of the other servers in the tank cluster. This work continues to build on the prior literature on the simulation and experimental work that has been conducted into immersion cooling and explores the impact of fluid properties on server cooling and the cooling of a compute cluster in an immersion cooling tank.

articleTitle: High Heat Flux Investigation of Copper-Nickel Alloys in R-1233zd(E) Pool Boiling
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: This study presents an in-depth investigation of pool boiling performance on a copper-nickel substrate, focusing on high heat flux applications crucial in industries such as petrochemical processing. Despite copper-nickel alloys having lower thermal conductivity than pure copper, their enhanced corrosion resistance is advantageous for high-temperature operations. We conducted experiments using R-1233zd(E) dielectric refrigerant at 1.5 and 2.0 bar saturation pressures, examining boiling on a flat, smooth circular surface with heat fluxes ranging from 1.3 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 9.3 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It has been observed that the heat transfer coefficient of a smooth specimen increases by approximately 5 to 25% when the pressure changes from 1.5 to 2 bar. Meanwhile, the boiling curve's wall superheat showed a reduction ranging from about 0.86 K to 1.52 K. A significant aspect of the study was the use of high-speed cameras, which captured the nuances of bubble generation, growth, and coalescence during the boiling process. These observations were crucial in observing bubble departure diameters at different operating conditions. This study provides valuable insights into boiling mechanisms, particularly bubble dynamics and heat transfer.

articleTitle: LPV ROM Based Analysis Approach to Optimize Thermal Dissipation Performance of an Automotive ECU
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving automotive industry, Electronic Control Units (ECUs) are crucial in ensuring the optimal performance and safety of modern vehicles. With the increasing complexity of vehicle electronics, the demand for efficient and reliable thermal management has grown substantially. Among the various heat dissipation methods available, forced convection methods with fans are widely adopted, but for effective thermal control, fan flow needs to be dynamically regulated. This research focuses on the thermal modelling and optimization of an automotive ECU system using an enhanced Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) Reduced Order Model (ROM) method to predict fan flow for dynamic thermal management. The research begins by developing a detailed Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model depicting ECU thermal behavior, but challenges arise when multiple transient simulations are needed. Traditional methods have limitations in computational time, especially when dealing with various design configurations and operating conditions. Hence, ROMs are introduced as efficient approximations of the complex CFD model, retaining essential thermal characteristics while reducing simulation time. The prototype model consists of a housing unit with an Application Processor (AP), Microcontroller Unit (MCU), and Double Data Rate (DDR) packages, optimized by a forced-convection system with two fans. The enhanced LPV ROM method integrates these fans into a single flow parameter, generating step response profiles at different flow rates. The method continuously computes and provides temperature data, adapting to varying power inputs. Python-based control logic is implemented to regulate the flow rate based on output temperature. Additionally, a temperature-fan flow rate transfer function is established through CFD analysis, correlating the relationship between thermal packages and fan flow. A comprehensive comparison between the enhanced LPV ROM method and detailed CFD analysis reveals that the former method produces results within an acceptable temperature error margin while significantly reducing the computational time. Employing the enhanced LPV ROM, multiple transient simulations are conducted, laying the foundation for a responsive Dynamic Thermal Management (DTM) system. Moreover, the developed process, combining CFD and ROMs, has broad applications across coolant-based electronic systems, for both the automotive industry and other engineering domains. It provides a robust framework for elevating thermal management practices, enhancing efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of critical electronic components.

articleTitle: Dynamic Testing and Simulation of Chassis Attached Remote Modular Heat Sink
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: The increasing mass of a Remote Modular Heat Sink (RMHS) in a chassis increases general system structural risks, especially failures under dynamic stress. This work designed a 1 Rack Unit (1U) server chassis representing the key structural ingredients and investigated RMHS dynamic behavior inside the chassis. The RMHS remote module is attached to the chassis base pan directly. Different RMHS designs are analyzed with the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and compared through stiffness analysis. Shock tests are performed on a chassis with different heatsink configurations and masses. Dynamic response of the RMHS is measured and compared with that of a conventional heatsink on Central Processing Unit (CPU) package. Vibration tests are performed with different chassis configurations. The FEA models are established at chassis level with RMHS, which are correlated to the test data through modal analysis.

articleTitle: Enclosure for data processing unit electronics (DPU) with integrated phase-change thermal capacitor for space applications - a design overview
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In the article authors describe areas of phase change material utilisation with special emphasize of the data processing unit electronics for the space applications. As a preliminary activity thermal numerical model was created with set of boundary conditions representing duty cycle of the electronics. The simulation results were used as a base for preparation of experiment. These two sets of results were described independently and finally compared with detailed evaluation. Results are promising for the electronic devices development integrated with the phase-change thermal capacitor for improvement its lifetime and capability.

articleTitle: Experimental study of a 3D-printed wick condenser for enhanced condensation heat transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Existing methods for improving condensation heat transfer face challenges with low surface tension liquids that exhibit strong wetting properties. These liquids tend to condense as thin films, leading to suboptimal thermal performance. This study investigates the effectiveness of a novel 3D-printed wick condenser in enhancing the condensation heat transfer rate of low surface tension fluids. An experimental test facility is developed to compare the heat dissipation performance of the 3D-printed wick condenser with a plain surface. The wick condenser, 3D-printed using GRCop-42 with an effective thermal conductivity of 344 W/m-K at room temperature, demonstrates remarkable heat flux capabilities. For example, at a subcooling of 10.5°C, the new 3D-printed wick condenser achieves a heat flux of about 61 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with the low-surface-tension fluid HFE-7100, representing a 4-fold improvement compared to a plain copper surface. The insights gained from this study open up exciting possibilities for the development of next-generation condensation surface technologies that offer unprecedented heat transfer rates, especially for liquids with complete wetting behavior.

articleTitle: Optimization of Structurally Enhanced Solder Transient Liquid Phase Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: High temperature packaging technologies are a necessity for high temperature capable devices. SAC305 solder has an operational limit of 174℃ imposed by creep effects which aligns well with current junction temperature limits of 175℃. Wide band gap semiconductor materials have the potential to reach junction temperatures of up to 800℃ that are not currently attainable with significant reliability. Capitalizing on this potential will requires substrates and attachments that can operate well beyond the current 175℃ standard. Silver sintering pastes have received widespread interest as a high temperature attachment alternative. However, the process requires high pressure bonding in an inert environment to achieve acceptable bond quality. Transient liquid phase (TLP) sintering is capable of good bond quality without pressure requirements but suffers from low thermal conductivity and only slightly reduced cost compared to silver sintering. SAC305 solder contains the same constituent materials for TLP as available copper-tin TLP sintering paste. By introducing engineered surface structures into the bond, intermetallic formation can be accelerated producing a bond similar to TLP sintering but in an ambient environment and for reduced cost. While this process has been demonstrated, it has not yet been optimized. Currently bonds are formed using a 75 μm stencil on substrate surface structures 24 μm tall, covering 19% of the bonding area. The process takes about 4 hours not including the formation of surface structures. This study will center on the effects of stencil thickness and coating methods. Samples will be analyzed by scanning acoustic microscopy, die shear testing and cross sectional scanning acoustic microscopy.

articleTitle: Modeling Flow Boiling Utilizing Machine Learning Vision Data
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Flow boiling is a very efficient configuration for meeting the high heat dissipation demands of thermal management systems. However, the lack of a clear understanding of physics affecting two-phase flow has limited its wide implementation across thermal systems. Recently, novel machine learning vision tools have been developed to capture physical feature information during subcooled flow boiling in a rectangular channel with single-sided heating. These features include local and averaged, as well as transient and steady-state statistical data on void fraction, vapor-liquid voids, interfacial behaviors, and liquidsolid wall wetting front areas. In this study, this data is used to model performance parameters in flow boiling. The statistical information relating to void fraction, bubble behaviors, interfacial waviness, and wetting fronts is analyzed and correlated with heat transfer coefficients, and critical heat flux. The data is used in combination with traditional control-volume-based theoretical modeling techniques to capture the relationship between the parameter of interest and the input parameters. The data on channel void fraction and wetting front areas are used to improve theoretical models predicting heat transfer coefficient. The data on interfacial behaviors and wetting front areas is to improve mechanistic model predicting critical heat flux. With this work, a new approach to utilizing machine vision data is proposed and validated.

articleTitle: Micro Scale Phosphor Particles in an LED Package: Heat Transfer, Fluid Dynamics, Optical Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Use of photoluminescent materials in combination with colored Light Emitting diodes (LEDs) to generate white light is a common practice in general lighting applications. However, this color conversion comes with an added heat generation issue that reduces the performance of LED-based white light systems. This investigation combines optical and thermofluid models to iteratively analyze system's optothermal behavior. Employing commercial CFD software for thermal modeling and Mie scattering theory with Monte Carlo ray tracing for optical behavior. This study examines the impact of particle concentration on heat generation and Nusselt number of a single blue LED chip. Results demonstrated a direct relationship between higher particle concentration and increased fluid temperature and velocity. Visual representations depicted temperature and velocity distributions, revealing system variations. This iterative approach, as the first in class, provides valuable insight into particle-fluid dynamics and heat transfer, offering a framework for optimizing thermal performance in similar systems with multi-chip LEDs. In these simulations, an observed change in Nu number demonstrates an approximate increase of 1.5 times compared to that of a liquid without any particles.

articleTitle: 3D-printed Ceramic Oscillating Heat Pipes for Improved Electronic Thermal Management
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Oscillating heat pipes (OHP) are attractive thermal management solutions as they can passively and effectively transfer heat between the hot evaporator and cold condenser sides. They rely on sensible and latent heat associated with the fast-oscillating liquid plugs and vapor slugs. However, existing metallic OHPs are not ideal solutions for electronic cooling applications and/or high-temperature processes due to high thermal expansion mismatch and low melting temperatures. Alternatively, ceramic oscillating heat pipes are deemed promising for semiconductor cooling applications and/or high-temperature heat transfer processes due to their suitable coefficient of thermal expansion, negligible electrical conductivity, high melting point, and chemical stability. However, the fabrication and/or machining of ceramic OHPs has been challenging due to low ductility combined with high hardness and high melting temperatures. Also, ceramic heat exchangers and heat pipes oftentimes suffer from a through-plane leakage inherent to a powder-based manufacturing process. Here, a hermetically sealed alumina-based OHP is fabricated through an extrusion-based ceramic 3D printing approach (i.e., the robocasting method). The 3D-printed alumina OHP consists of 20 milli-channels with a flow length of 80 mm and a 2.2 mm by 2 mm cross-sectional area. The thermal performance of the 3D-printed alumina OHP was examined at a filling ratio of 46% with methanol as a working fluid at varying heat load capacities. It was found that the thermal resistance of the OHP is 1°C/W, which is 65% lower than that of the uncharged state (i.e., 0% filling ratio) at a heat input of 45W. Additionally, the infrared images show a more uniform temperature distribution across the ceramic OHP compared with the uncharged state owing to the pulsating effect. The findings obtained from this study can serve as a foundation for future electronic cooling applications that involve the use of ceramic oscillating heat pipes (OHPs).

articleTitle: A Heat Transfer Study of Indirect Two-phase Cold Plate Liquid Cooling Design for Data Center
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Liquid cooling technology for sustainable data center deployment has been mainly driven by increasingly higher Thermal Design Power (TDP) microprocessors, sustainability regulation and enforcement, and higher compute power demand from the edge, especially the harsh edge environment. As more pilot deployment cases of both cold plate and immersion cooling solutions of single phase unveiled, liquid cooling adoption in data center is in the spotlight with more confidences gained from the industry. Two phase cold plate solution due to its latent heat dissipation design mechanism where working fluid of lower conductivity and boiling point used, can be naturally manufactured with compact size ingredients such as quick connector and pipeline for the scenarios that demand continuously increasing flow rate of working fluid for cooling the high heat flux processor clusters. However, designing improved heat dissipation surfaces for two-phase thermal convection through simulation alone poses challenges. This study, using the novel refrigerant R-1336mzz(Z), aims to fabricate various enhanced heat dissipation surfaces under manufacturable conditions for verifying their heat transfer performance. Techniques such as Skived Fin, sintering, and sandblasting, along with aluminum surfaces, are explored. The objective is to identify process technologies applicable under different power conditions of data center processors to meet productization requirements.

articleTitle: Capillary Suction for Evaporative Cooling
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Dissipating heat from high power systems and components is a challenge that comes with miniaturization of any kind of electronics. Among other cooling solutions, two-phase cooling is seen as a technique with high potential thanks to heat transfer by latent heat. When flow boiling is the main mechanism in two-phase cooling, flow instabilities may appear and generate issues to control the entire flow. Such concerns can be avoided with evaporative cooling. More specifically, the combination of evaporative cooling with a designed porous system can significantly improve the heat exchanges. The designed porous system presented here, thanks to the hierarchical structure of its pores can deliver the coolant by capillary action, removing any need for a pumping system. Nevertheless, in such configurations, the flow of liquid throughout the porous network competes with friction along the channel walls, calling for a better understanding of the effect of the pore network structure on the performance of the evaporation process. Here, we fix the porosity, and we investigate how the pores should be connected for maximum heat exchanges when the coolant flows by capillarity. We theoretically show that the pore network is a structure whose features are highly hierarchical and dendritic, and propose configurations allowing vapor to be generated at the very exit of the porous network for a given heat flux. We developed a numerical model that accounts for the flow transport through the porous configuration and for evaporation at the outlet of the capillary network. For the same porosity and pore radius, the heat transfer coefficient is higher when the number of pores is higher. As we increase the input heat flux, the heat transfer coefficient is higher. For the two different structures we proposed, the radius ratio exponent shows different behavior when we increase the porosity. Finally, this study helps understand the relationship between capillary-driven evaporative cooling and the architecture of porous media for the cooling of electronics.

articleTitle: Accelerated Test For Thermal Grease Pump-out
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Thermal greases are highly filled silicone suspensions utilized in electronics to improve heat dissipation. A thermal grease fills in the narrow gap (~20-200 µm) between the chip and the heat sink improving the heat conductivity of the assembly. In most applications, the heating and cooling cycles generate warpage owing to the disparity in thermal expansion coefficients between the chip and the heat sink. This warpage induces stresses on the thermal grease displacing it outwards from the narrow gap where it was initially located. In some instances, and after several heating and cooling cycles, the thermal grease is irreversibly displaced out from the assembly, a phenomenon called pump-out. In this work, we present a new accelerated method to evaluate anti pump-out performance, which is capable of replicating results of standard pump-out tests while also providing greater insight on material property requirements impacting performance. The accelerated method isolates the mechanical deformation from the thermal stresses which improves repeatability and sensitivity. The accelerated method has a maximum duration of 2h per sample, which is ~100x faster than standard CPU/GPU stress tests. Last, the usefulness and accuracy of the method will be illustrated through a series of practical examples.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Reliability Evaluation of Additively Printed Temperature and Humidity Sensor on Additively Manufactured ABS Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In the field of printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing, additive manufacturing is attracting people in the various industries due to its cost-effectiveness and flexibility. Additive manufacturing, with its software-driven design, offers greater flexibility and ease in implementing design changes, marking a more efficient PCB production. These methods excel in their ability to work with various substrates and forms, on various flexible hybrid electronics (FHE). Temperature and humidity sensors created through additive printing can be considered candidate of in-mold electronics offering compactness and versatility in printing on diverse materials. However, challenges arise in ensuring their reliability under varying conditions such as extreme hygrothermal aging and high strain folding. In this regard, addressing these issues involves refining printing techniques, process recipes, improving the encapsulation of sensing materials and multi-layer build up. This research concentrates on fabricating temperature and humidity sensors on an additively manufactured ABS substrate, employing an additive printing approach of printed circuits with Ag/AgCl ink and polyimide dielectric with in-mold component attachment. The study aims to improve the reliability of these sensors, developing industry-standard recipes for additive fabrication and evaluating sensor reliability. Utilizing a Voltera printer, the study involves direct write (D-write) printing of multi-layered sensors and circuits on ABS which is fabricated via additive manufacturing technique as well in a lab environment. Moreover, this research develops in-mold attachment of the device component and Z-axis multi-layered buildup of dielectric material. Additionally, the research investigates the relationship between the number of printed layers and characteristics like thickness, resistance, porosity, and encapsulation or lamination. The study measures the sensors’ resistance variance to temperature and humidity changes, examining their non-linearity, hysteresis and long-term stability under high temperature and humidity condition. The findings display the fabricated sensing board are properly working with high precision.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization of Contemporary Electrical Insulation Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Electrically insulating materials are integral components in many devices including coatings for electric wires and cables, circuit boards, electric machines, and high-voltage devices. Within electrical machines like motors, common electrical insulating components are extensively used to isolate components at different voltages. In this paper, we focus on slot liners that isolate the copper windings from the stator within an electric motor. Although manufacturers routinely provide the electrical and mechanical properties of these materials, their thermal properties, including thermal conductivity, are not often reported. However, their thermal properties are critical for understanding the temperatures of operating devices. To address this gap, this research characterizes the thermophysical properties of different commercially-available sheet-like insulation materials commonly employed as slot liners and other similar materials for benchmarking. We report essential thermophysical properties (in-plane thermal conductivity, through-plane thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat capacity). These parameters, while often overlooked in datasheets, are crucial to gauging the thermal performance of the (electrical) insulation materials in such thermally demanding applications. This new data provides insight required to improve the selection of electrically insulating materials for applications in electric machines.

articleTitle: Evaluating Shear Properties of Individual Solder Joints in Ball Grid Arrays: The Impact of Silver (Ag) and Bismuth (Bi) Content
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: The solder interconnections represent the weakest element in electronic assemblies. The reliability of the solder joint is significantly affected by the mechanical bond formed between the bulk joint and the printed circuit board pads. Shear testing is a widely employed quick method for evaluating the strength of the joint, thus ensuring the integrity of the electronic assembly. Shear testing involves the consideration of several parameters, including shear height, solder alloy composition, surface finish, solder mask, and shear strain rate. This study investigates the impact of Ag and Bi content on the shear properties of third-generation solder alloys. Individual solder spheres were assembled on Solder-Mask-Define (SMD) pads using tacky flux. Solder alloys include SAC with 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4% silver (Ag) and SAC-Bi with 1% and 2% bismuth. All tests were conducted at a fixed strain rate of 0.1 sec<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The Instron 5948 Micro Tester, equipped with a customized fixture, was used to execute shear tests on individual solder joints. Shear stress-strain curves were captured for every test, and subsequent calculations were conducted to determine shear strength. The results revealed that increasing the Bi content increases the ultimate shear strength for the OSP finish but decreases it for the ENIG surface finish. Increasing the Ag content increases the strength due to precipitate hardening. Various failure modes were observed, including ductile failure, brittle failure, and a combination of both.

articleTitle: The Effect of Conformal Coating on QFN Assembly Reliability: Thermal Cycling and HALT
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Commercial industry started to use conformal coating for addressing Restriction of Hazardous Substances (ROHS) tin whisker concerns at assembly level whereas its use has been the norm for high-reliability applications. Thicker coatings better mitigate tin whisker, but it may add additional significant vertical mismatch stresses resulting in premature solder-joint failures under thermal cycling. The stresses are significantly increase in an extreme cold environment, e.g., deep-space missions, because increase in rigidity; therefore, it is of concern for these applications. This paper presents the effect of standard single- and double- thickness of polyurethane coating on various sizes of Quad Flat No-Lead (QFN) solder joint assemblies. The two thicknesses evaluated under thermal cycling tests and through an innovative Highly Accelerated Life Testing (HALT) method.The temperature cycling was performed from –55°C to +125°C for the two thickness of coatings. The HALT was performed under 50g three-dimensional random vibration at −100°C, based on an analytical stress model that showed solder joints will be in inelastic stress condition. The HALT step followed with thermal shock cycling in the range of −100°C to 125°C to detect possible latent defects due to a priori vibration. Monitoring focused on four daisy-chain QFN assemblies during HALT, followed by manual verification at RT after testing. The thermal cycle results are presented in Weibull plots, depicting the effect of conformal coating. The uncoated and coated QFN failures under sequential HALT and thermal shock cycles are also presented.

articleTitle: Thermal Testing and Analysis of On-the-Market Smartwatches
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: The smartwatch is rapidly becoming one of the most popular consumer electronics devices on the market. Tech giants such as Apple, Samsung, and Google are releasing new products each year with upgrades that include health monitoring, water proofing, crash detection, and more. The smartwatch industry had a market size and share of 28.5 billion dollars in 2021. It is expected to grow to 80.1 billion dollars by 2028.Thermal management plays a key role in the design and safety of wearable devices. Wearables need to be able to process large amounts of information. This can lead to periods of high-power dissipation. Since the smart watch is in direct contact with the skin, the temperature has to be carefully controlled. If the power dissipation of a smartwatch is not managed correctly, it can cause discomfort or harm to the wearer.Large companies are struggling to successfully address the thermal design requirements of these products. On March 2, 2022, Fitbit announced a recall of its Ionic smartwatches. Their recall notice cautioned that the battery within the watch was prone to overheating and could cause a burn to its users. In September of the same year, some users reported that their Samsung Galaxy Watch 2 gave them 3rd degree burns while they were sleeping.This presentation analyzes the thermal design of various smartwatches on the market by performing thermal testing, teardown, and thermal modeling simulations. The simulations were done using Siemens’ Simcenter FloEFD software. This effort was coordinated with Siemens to demonstrate the capabilities of the Siemens FloEFD CFD software.The smartwatches chosen for this study were the Apple Watch Series 8 and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 5. These products are representative of the latest and most advanced designs from two of the world’s leading technology companies. These products are also of interest as they can monitor heart rate, electrocardiogram, blood oxygen, and skin temperature. Each of these products also have access to an extensive library of apps. These apps allow for a variety of use cases that can be replicated in a lab setting.First, these smartwatches will go through thermal testing for different use scenarios with thermocouples applied to different points of interest, such as the battery, human contact points, and the main processor. Then, the smartwatches will go through a teardown process to weigh and measure each individual component of the device. Finally, a 3D CAD model will be built with appropriate material and thermal properties, using the results of the teardown and testing. Since access to precise power dissipation data is unavailable, the temperature profiles of the device for different use cases were used to estimate component power dissipations. After the modeling was completed, Simcenter FloEFD was used to perform CFD simulations.Comparison of the results of simulation and testing enables the authors to understand how the design of each smartwatch dissipates heat and which design features function better.

articleTitle: Accurate Temperature Prediction of Complex Die Power Maps using Quadtree Based Surrogate
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Predicting die temperature distribution based on complex die power maps is not uncommon but is frequently detached from any in situ analysis in a 3D conjugate heat transfer simulation. In a CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) simulation simplifying assumptions regarding the die power distribution are typically imposed that balance the usefulness of the temperature prediction with simulation speed. To predict the most accurate die temperatures a simulation that includes the detailed die power map, the IC (integrated circuit) package and the surrounding environment is required.This paper discusses an approach to efficiently simulating a die with thousands of discrete power sources in a conjugate heat transfer CFD simulation. Discrete power sources are mapped to an n x m array of sources to perform a preliminary analysis to produce a surrogate temperature map. The temperature map is subdivided using Quadtree image processing to determine the areas of the die for computational refinement. At each increasing Quadtree level, the physical accuracy of the discrete source representation is increased. The highest Quadtree level, that contains the highest temperature, is modeled with discrete sources.A validation of the methodology will be discussed which will compare simulations of a die power map representation with explicit discrete sources to the Quadtree refinement approach. The Quadtree approach will then be applied to a die power map with many discrete sources that would be impractical for discrete representation.

articleTitle: Analytical prediction of thermal performance and flow non-uniformity of manifold microchannel heat sinks
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: An analytical model has been proposed and validated to accurately predict the thermal performance and the flow non-uniformity of the manifold microchannel (MMC) heat sinks. To this end, one-dimensional governing equations are derived from the integral relations of momentum and energy over appropriately-defined two separate control volumes. Specifically, a control volume for the momentum balance is defined in the fluid region, including a dividing flow junction where the main fluid stream branches off from the manifold to the microchannels. A control volume for the energy balance in the solid region is defined so that it incorporates an individual microchannel and its solid substrate. The derived one-dimensional governing equations are solved without introducing any fitting parameters. By solving these equations, the flow distribution among the microchannels and the temperature distribution within the solid substrate are estimated. In order to verify the proposed model, a series of 3-D numerical simulation is conducted over a wide range of geometric parameters and operating conditions. This range includes the channel aspect ratio (AR) from 3 to 15, the Reynolds number (Re<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">man</inf>) at the manifold inlet from 560 to 3190, the dimensionless hydraulic flow length (x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) from 0.012 to 0.123, and the dimensionless thermal flow length (x*) from 0.002 to 0.023. It is shown that the model provides an accurate prediction of the thermal performance and the flow non-uniformity of MMC heat sinks: the total thermal resistance and the coefficient of variation (CV) of the flow distribution among the microchannels are estimated within the root mean square percentage error (RMSPE) of 6% and 23% for 51 data points. The results emphasize that the non-uniform flow distribution among the microchannels should be taken into account for accurately predicting the thermal performance of MMC heat sinks. By accounting for the non-uniformity in the flow distribution, the significant improvement of the prediction accuracy is made over the earlier model with an error reduction of 81%.

articleTitle: The Effect of Bi Content and Strain Rate on Tensile Properties of SnAgCu-Bi Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: In response to the lead prohibition within the electronic industry, SAC alloys have become the benchmark for lead-free solder. However, several dopants, such as bismuth (Bi), designed to enhance the mechanical properties of these alloys, have been introduced into the market. This study aims to assess the impact of Bi content in SAC-Bi alloys and strain rates on the tensile properties of vacuum-casted Bismuth-doped bulk SAC-Bi alloy specimens, specifically SAC405-0%Bi, SAC405-1% Bi, SAC405-2% Bi, and SAC405-3% Bi. Before conducting the tensile tests, X-ray analysis was performed to ensure the absence of voids in the specimens. The specimens were tested in a controlled environment using an Instron 5948 Micro Tester. By analyzing the stress-strain plots, essential mechanical parameters, including the ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and yield stress, were derived. A comparative analysis was conducted under different Bi content and strain rates of 0.001, 0.01, and 1 sec<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The results demonstrated that the inclusion of Bi enhanced the mechanical properties of SAC alloys. The observations revealed a direct correlation between the concentration of Bi and the magnitude of improvement in mechanical properties. The higher content of Bi resulted in more substantial enhancements, with an average increase of 13% in UTS, and 11% in yield stress. For all the alloys, the UTS showed an increase at higher strain rates, with a more pronounced effect observed in the alloys without Bi.

articleTitle: Applied Machine Learning for Enterprise SSDs Operating Curve Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 23rd IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm)
abstract: Enterprise solid-state drives (eSSDs) are used in data centers due to their high capacity and performance. The operating curve, which is an important eSSD parameter, defines their operating region.
